rounds.text: United Leasing & Industries Ltd trades at an extreme valuation that is entirely disconnected from its fundamental reality, carrying a filed P/E of 114x and an even more egregious data provider P/E of 340x against a sector benchmark of just 18.92x [E1, E6]. This premium pricing is fundamentally unjustified given that the company generates a negligible return on assets of 0.23% compared to a sector benchmark of 2.22% and offers a zero dividend yield [E4, E8]. Furthermore, the business is experiencing a severe top-line contraction, evidenced by a 3-year compounded sales growth of -12%, a trailing twelve-month decline of -9%, and a stark YoY sales drop of -40% [E16, E17, E64]. Expectations are dangerously running ahead of delivery, as evidenced by price growth exceeding profit growth by 11% while earnings growth decelerates and sales plummet [E54, E65]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong historical compounded sales growth over 5 and 10-year periods alongside YoY profit growth above 20% [E14, E15, E62].

Conceded: the filed P/E sits at 114x and the data provider P/E at 340x against a sector benchmark of 18.92x [E1, E6]. However, focusing exclusively on earnings multiples ignores the asset backing and historical execution of the firm, which trades at a modest price-to-book of 1.48x on a book value of 23 rupees per share [E2]. The bear highlights recent top-line contractions of -12% over 3 years and -9% over the trailing twelve months, yet overlooks the exceptional long-term wealth creation engine reflected in a 10-year compounded sales growth of 29% and a 5-year compounded sales growth of 46% [E14, E15, E16, E17]. Furthermore, the bear's alarm over a 40% YoY sales drop and decelerating earnings ignores the scanner's explicit screening reason confirming that year-over-year profit growth exceeded 20% [E62, E64, E65]. The stock also sits near the bottom of its 52-week range at just 22% of its span, meaning much of the cyclical top-line pressure is already priced into a micro-cap valuation of 10.2 crore rupees [E3, E5]. Finally, while the bear points to a zero dividend yield and low ROA against sector benchmarks, these metrics fail to capture a business undergoing turnaround strength supported by active profit growth screens [E4, E8, E62].

Conceded: 10-year compounded sales growth is 29% and 5-year compounded sales growth is 46% [E14, E15]. Conceded: the price-to-book is 1.48x [E2]. However, pointing to historical growth ignores severe recent deterioration, specifically a 3-year compounded sales contraction of -12%, a TTM contraction of -9%, and a screen warning of a 40% YoY sales drop [E16, E17, E64]. The bull dismisses valuation by citing a modest book value, but ignores that the data provider pegs the P/B at 3.41x against a sector benchmark of 1.26x, while the actual P/E sits at a staggering 114x from filed statements and 340x against a sector benchmark of 18.92x [E1, E6, E7]. The argument that low positioning at 22% of the 52-week range prices in cyclical pressure is contradicted by signal engine warnings that price growth exceeds profit growth by 11%, showing expectations are running ahead of delivery [E5, E54]. Finally, invoking profit growth screens does not erase an anemic ROA of 0.23% versus a 2.22% sector benchmark, nor does it excuse a 0.00% dividend yield for a micro-cap valued at ₹ 10.2 Cr [E3, E4, E8, E62].
